correctness.rationale: Conditioning on \(M_n\sim\operatorname{Bin}(n,\lambda/n)\) gives \(M_n\Rightarrow\operatorname{Poisson}(\lambda)\). For fixed \(m\ge2\), uniform cut locations yield Dirichlet gap proportions and the uniformly seeded component is a size-biased \(\operatorname{Beta}(2,m-1)\) gap. The Poisson mixture sums exactly to the stated atom and density; differentiating the CDF proves stochastic ordering. The bounded statistic \(Y_n^2\) converges in expectation, and its integral gives the stated welfare fraction.
